text.text_excerpt: I booked this for date day with Hubby and the whole booking process was easy. You book and pay online for the class you would like to attend. We opted for the Sunday afternoon class and we were paining the bayou. I checked in and received a free mug which was nice. We got there and the guys that work there are pretty friendly. ( parking is free on Sunday , just an FYI). The easels and table was set up and we just chose our seats. There is free coffee which tastes really nice. The art instructor takes you through the painting step by step and it was quite easy to follow. I am an artist and painting is not new to me. I. LOVE. THIS. PLACE. i don't do wine, but I do however, do liquor, water, tea, and/or coffee. Went on Sunday, because I loved the photo they were doing. I arrived 30 minutes early, as suggested (FYI free parking on Sundays). When you walk in, there is a room full of long tables with easels on both sides (facing center of tables). To the right is the front desk where you check in. They give you the easel (which has handy drawings on it if you're drawing a person), and you go choose your spot. I chose the back room because it was cooler back there. There was fun music playing in each of the rooms. What fun place! We've had 2 medium-large sized parties here and they've done a great job both times. You pick what date you want on the calendar (there's a picture of what painting is being offered that day) and each person pays $45 bucks when they get there. The first time we brought our own wine + got a few free bottles from them, but because we booked a 2nd party during the end of the initial one - we got a free case of wine for the next party! It's not the best wine on the planet, but who cares. After the 5th glass or so, the artistry really comes out!
